content:
Arjun Desai: Quick q for INT8 profile policy + the perf sprint. What are we treating as “required” calibration for INT8 defaults? I’m seeing mixed guidance (static vs dynamic, per-channel vs per-tensor). Also any known model-family quirks we should encode as guardrails (long context, MoE, Qwen-ish outliers, etc.). Want to avoid us enabling INT8 broadly and then getting quality tickets.

Jonas Weber: For “default enable” we should assume static activation-aware INT8 (SmoothQuant-ish) w/ representative calibration prompts. Pure weight-only INT8 can be ok for some models but it’s not consistently safe across our hosted traffic mix.

Jonas Weber: Minimum bar I’d like for hosted defaults:
- calibration set from benchmark-suite v3 prompt pool (not synthetic random tokens)
- includes long-prefill cases (>=8k tokens) + tool/JSON structured output prompts
- measure: quick sanity suite + spot-check win-rate on a small eval slice
- and importantly: compare to FP16/BF16 baseline for the same model version + tokenizer

Priyanka Bose: +1. The calibration “shape” matters too: if we calibrate only on 1k context and then serve 16k, we can get activation outliers in attention proj and MLP up_proj that blow up. Seen this w/ Llama-2/3 family and some Mistral variants.

Priyanka Bose: Concrete knobs we’ve been using:
- per-channel weight quant (always)
- activation scales: static per-tensor (more stable) vs per-token dynamic (can be slower / kernel coverage issues)
- group size: 128 tends to be a sweet spot; 64 sometimes better quality but perf hit depending on kernel

Claire Dubois: Can we be explicit about “calibration dataset” size? People keep using 128 prompts and calling it good.

Jonas Weber: For sign-off I’m ok w/ ~512–1k prompts for calibration (fast), but the key is distribution coverage not raw count. I’d rather see 300 prompts that cover:
- chat (short/med)
- summarization w/ long prefill
- code gen
- retrieval-style (dense context + short answer)
- structured output (JSON)

Jonas Weber: Then eval sanity suite (the lightweight one in eval-harness PR-519) should run on at least 50–100 golden prompts per model.

Rina Kobayashi: From harness side: our INT8 path currently expects static scales baked into the model artifact (or sidecar). Dynamic scales break some of the end-to-end runner assumptions + they don’t hit the same kernel dispatch on H100/A100. So if ML says “dynamic ok” but runtime can’t benchmark it apples-to-apples, we’ll end up with confusing results.

Grace Kim: +1. Also kernel constraints: the INT8 matmul path has shape/alignment guardrails (k % 16 etc). If calibration generates scales for a layer we end up falling back (because shape unsupported), perf numbers are misleading and quality comparisons are noisy (mixed mode within a forward pass).

Isabella Rossi: For microbench, we saw certain hidden sizes (esp odd multiples) trigger fallback more on A100 than H100. So please call out model families where layer dims / head dims are “weird” so we can flag them in the policy.

Arjun Desai: Helpful. On quirks: any known “do not INT8” categories? (MoE, long-context, etc.)

Priyanka Bose: MoE: higher risk. Mixtral-style gating + expert MLPs can be sensitive depending on quant scheme. Weight-only INT8 often shows quality drift in routing for some prompts (esp code). If we do INT8 there, I’d require eval sign-off + potentially restrict to short context.

Jonas Weber: Long-context: risk is less about “INT8 always bad” and more about calibration mismatch. If we calibrate w/ long-prefill included, it’s usually fine. If we don’t, we can get:
- degraded adherence to JSON schema
- increased repetition / truncation
- worse factual consistency for RAG-style prompts

Claire Dubois: Also note: quality regressions often look like “small” perplexity changes but are very visible in tool-calling reliability. So for default enablement, tool/structured-output prompts should be treated as first-class.

Olivia Grant: Adding: online signals we can watch during canary:
- function/tool call parse failure rate
- JSON validation failures
- “empty tool args” and “invalid enum” counts
- user-visible retry rate (client 4xx/5xx + model errors)
These spike earlier than generic win-rate metrics.

Rina Kobayashi: For perf/quality trade-off, one more runtime detail: INT8 can improve decode tokens/s but sometimes increases TTFT if we introduce extra dequant/scale loads in prefill. So calibrations that force more layers into INT8 vs fallback can affect TTFT more than folks expect.

Grace Kim: Specific family quirks we’ve hit:
- Qwen-ish: outliers in attention proj; needs calibration prompts with multilingual + code mixed to stabilize.
- Llama-3 long context: KV-cache related alignment + quant noise shows up more in decode on 8k+; include long-prefill and long-decode samples.
- Some Mistral variants: smaller head_dim (or different rope scaling) interacts w/ kernel coverage; not directly calibration but affects which layers get INT8 kernels.

Arjun Desai: So proposal for policy doc:
1) Default INT8 requires static activation-aware calibration; no “dynamic only” profiles as default.
2) Calibration set must include long-prefill + structured output prompts.
3) MoE models require explicit eval sign-off and potentially “INT8 off by default”.
Sound right?

Jonas Weber: Yes. Add: any model where runtime falls back >X% layers (or >Y% matmul ops) should not ship as “INT8 default” even if quality is ok — perf benefit won’t be consistent and will cause confusion.

Isabella Rossi: We can provide that metric from bench artifacts if we tag kernel mode per op (Rina/Grace already adding tags). We should pick thresholds: e.g., <80% INT8 coverage => “experimental”.

Claire Dubois: Please also put a footnote: calibration is tied to a specific model hash + tokenizer + rope scaling config. We’ve had people reuse scales across minor model revs and then blame runtime.

Olivia Grant: Action item: I’ll write down the canary metrics checklist for “INT8 quality drift” to add to the rollout runbook.

Arjun Desai: Great. I’ll update the quant profile policy draft w/:
- required calibration composition (incl long-context + tool prompts)
- model-family caveats (MoE, Qwen-ish outliers)
- “coverage” guardrail so we don’t claim perf wins when runtime is in fallback.

Jonas Weber: Cool. Loop me + Claire for sign-off wording. If we’re going to enable defaults in hosted catalog, I want the doc to say “eval sign-off required” not “recommended.”

Rina Kobayashi: And loop runtime for the operational constraints (artifact format, where scales live, and what modes we can benchmark). I’ll drop a short note in #eng-runtime too.

Grace Kim: I’ll add a checklist item to the sprint daily notes: for each INT8 candidate profile, record calibration prompt set ID + context-length mix + kernel coverage stats. That’ll save us a lot of back-and-forth later.
